verification_report.summary:
The lower-barrier criterion variant and the full addition proof pass sequential verification under the explicitly accepted inputs. No critical errors or mathematical gaps were found. This verdict is conditional on the common-barrier criterion and weighted extended lower semicontinuity in common_barrier_compactness_01, and on the bounded subsolution theorem in bounded_subsolution_01: both final reports remain pending, and their conditional use was expressly authorized. A later note in the pending common-barrier audit flags an overbroad standalone monotone-sequence assertion: decreasing genuine potentials can converge identically to -infinity. That issue does not affect the referenced criterion or this proof, whose monotone sequences all have explicit genuine lower barriers. The completed singular_domination_01 and gauduchon_growth_01 reports have verdict correct. The book was read without modification.

For the criterion variant, the lower bound passes to the canonical L1 limit. The additional condition u preceq phi supplies u<=phi+K, so u has ordinary type phi. Every finite rooftop has the genuine competitor phi-C and common upper bound C. The accepted contact support and finite contact partition therefore give the exponential error bound 2^{1-j} without requiring the finite roofs or approximants to have type phi. Their decreasing limits p_j satisfy phi-C<=p_j<=u, and their increasing canonical limit p satisfies the same bounds. Thus these infinite roof limits have type phi. Monotone capacity convergence and weighted lower semicontinuity yield MAext(p)({p<u})=0. The competitor P_{delta theta}(phi)-C makes the smaller-background envelope of p genuine, while u preceq p follows from ordinary-type equivalence. Singular strict domination applies with coefficient zero and gives p=u. The decreasing upper tail envelopes and the original arbitrary-subsequence argument complete capacity convergence.

The common translation has the correct sign: replacing u,v by u-S,v-S changes mu to exp(lambda S)mu, and adding S to the resulting solution restores the original equation. Semipositivity preserves the bounded truncations. Positive mixed-product expansion gives MA(u_j)+MA(v_j)<=2^n MA(s_j), so mu_j has a bounded nonnegative Radon-Nikodym density relative to MA(s_j) for each fixed j. Individual bounded noncollapse supplies positive mass, meeting the bounded subsolution theorem's hypotheses. No uniform-in-j density or mass estimate is needed for that invocation.

Bounded exponential order gives a_j<=min(u_j,v_j)<=0. Truncation preserves |u_j-v_j|<=C. The choice D=C/2+(n/lambda)log 2 is correct: 2^{-n}exp(lambda D-lambda s_j)=exp(lambda C/2-lambda s_j) dominates each of exp(-lambda u_j) and exp(-lambda v_j). This proves the lower barrier a_j>=b_j>=w=(u+v)/2-D. The fixed genuine w has type phi and prevents L1 collapse. The extracted canonical limit satisfies w<=a<=min(u,v), hence a has type phi.

On E_j, locality gives mu_j=mu, and MA(a_j)<=mu there. The finite mu is non-pluripolar, so the accepted fixed-measure exponential convergence makes the shallow self-error vanish. Outside E_j, both a_j and a are <=-j. The exact finite-level equation gives MA(a_j)<=MA(u_j)+MA(v_j). Enlarging theta to a fixed Hermitian Omega and applying the accepted bounded-range estimate gives the error C exp(-j)(1+j)^r, with r=max(n-2,0), including r=0 in dimensions one and two. It tends to zero and establishes all hypotheses of the lower-barrier criterion. The bounded approximants are never assigned ordinary type phi.

The new localized passage is valid. For fixed T, wherever zeta_T=g_T(w) is nonzero, w,a_j,a>-2T. If j>2T, the complement of E_j has w<=a_j<=-j, so zeta_T vanishes there. Thus zeta_T MA(a_j)=zeta_T exp(lambda a_j)mu holds exactly. The proof needs the nonzero-weight locus; the wording 'on its support' entails no additional topological-support claim, since the weight is zero at the cutoff boundary. Replacing a_j by max(a_j,-2T) is justified by locality. These truncations are uniformly bounded and converge in capacity, so bounded Bedford-Taylor continuity with the fixed bounded quasi-continuous weight passes the left side. Fixed-measure exponential convergence passes the right side in total variation. This proves equality of the limiting weighted measures for each T.

Increasing the cutoffs exhausts the complement of the pluripolar pole set of genuine w. Both the positive extended Monge-Ampere measure and mu ignore this set. Monotone convergence on Borel sets therefore gives the full equation before finiteness of MAext(a) is known. Since a<=0, the equation implies MAext(a)(X)<=mu(X)<infinity. No global raw weak convergence, uniform approximating raw mass, BMP, PVP, or subtraction of infinite measures is assumed. Uniqueness follows by transferring smaller-background genuineness through bounded type changes and applying singular exponential order in both directions.

The required arXiv theorem search returned no matching statement; fallback web verification located the primary source. ALS26 Theorem 5.2 contains the cited addition construction. Its standing reference is a model potential, requiring both the envelope fixed-point property and a genuine smaller-background envelope; its Lemma 4.3 also assumes uniformly bounded approximating raw masses. These extra conditions are not imported here: the supplied criterion variant and localized passage were verified independently under the authorized inputs. The source's truncation estimate is j^n; the stronger exponent used here comes from gauduchon_growth_01. [ALS26, Definition 2.13, Lemma 4.3 and Theorem 5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339v1).
